instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead: cut the 1.25 lb pork shoulder into 3/4 inch cubes and put them in a bowl. Finely grate half of one onion, 2 of the garlic cloves and 1 1/2 tsp of the ginger over the pork. Add the 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tbsp of the cornstarch and 3 tbsp of the soy sauce, mix well with your hands, cover and refrigerate.

When you're ready to cook, rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 175°F and set a wire rack on a baking sheet for the fried pork.

Open the pineapple and drain it over a measuring cup, keeping 1/4 cup of the juice. In a bowl, stir together that juice, the 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup ketchup, 3/4 tsp Worcestershire sauce, the last 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 1/2 tsp oyster sauce and 2 tbsp of the cornstarch until the cornstarch dissolves. Stir in 3/4 cup water.
Cut the remaining onion and a half and both bell peppers into 1 inch pieces. Finely chop the last garlic clove and 1 tbsp of the remaining ginger. Measure out 1 1/2 cups of the pineapple chunks.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup of the cornstarch over the pork and mix it in. Leave it for 5 minutes, until the cornstarch turns damp and sticky.
Spread the last 3/4 cup cornstarch in a shallow dish. Roll the pork pieces in it, shake off the extra and pile them on a plate.

Pour the oil into a large saucepan so it's 1 inch deep, keeping 1 tbsp back for the stir fry. Heat it over medium high to 350°F. No thermometer? Drop in a piece of pork: it should sizzle hard straight away.

Fry the pork in 4 batches for 3 minutes each, until it's light golden. Don't crowd the pan. Lift each batch onto the rack with a slotted spoon. You're cooking the pork to 145°F, so if you have a thermometer, check a large piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when the center is white with no pink.

Turn the heat up a little so the oil gets to about 390°F. Fry the pork again in 2 batches for about 1 1/2 minutes each, until it's deep golden and crisp. Stand back a little. It will spatter. Put it back on the rack and slide the baking sheet into the oven.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil you kept back in a large skillet or wok over high. Add the onion and stir for 1 minute, until it starts to soften at the edges.
Add the chopped garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until they smell fragrant.
Add the peppers and stir for 2 minutes, until they're bright and a little charred but still crisp.
Stir the sauce again and pour it in with the pineapple. Let it bubble hard for about 2 minutes, until it's thick and glossy and a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a path for a second.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt or a splash more of the vinegar.
Add the pork and toss it for about 10 seconds, only until it's coated.
Serve straight away with the jasmine rice.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the pork the night before (at least 3 hours ahead)
method_notes: Both versions coat bite sized pork in cornstarch, fry it until golden, then toss it at the last second in a thick sauce of sugar, vinegar and ketchup. RecipeTin Eats marinates pork shoulder overnight with grated onion, garlic, ginger, soy and a little baking soda, coats it twice, double fries it, and stir fries onion, peppers and canned pineapple into the sauce. Omnivore's Cookbook keeps it closer to the Beijing style: tenderloin strips in an egg and cornstarch coating, shallow fried, in a sauce with Shaoxing wine and no vegetables. This one follows RecipeTin Eats, scaled up for 4 as a dinner, with the jasmine rice added.
